signature: :   "MICHAEL LEICHAM / SCHNEIDER IN WIENN 1738"; plate with figure of St. Michael.
provenance: Wien, Michaelerkirche; donated to the Museum in 1918 by A. Coletti.
literature: Schlosser 1920: 93, tafel XLIV (photo); Langwill 1974: 104; Stradner 1987: 106-16, fig. 4 (photo); *Vienna Catalogue; Stradner 1991: 112-13 (photos), 194 [with B & W photo of this instrument plus another and color photo of bell of 1738 instrument. Stradner 1991: 112 says cat. No is 191. Color photo shows bell of 1738 inst., with bell visible; adjacent is bell bow and bell stay of the other instrument? or is it the same instr, and the two parts have been disengaged? Cat. Not given for other inst. Is it a Leichamschneider? B&W photos also shows a case.] In “catalog” at end of book, p. 294, info is given on the two instruments. Stradner 1991 cont: p. 294 gives description and measurements. Stradner 1991 isn’t clear. Two trombones are pictured. Stradner says, on p. 294: “Das Paar Tenorposaunen, von denen eine hier vorliegt und die andere derzeit in der österreichischen Nationalbibliothek ausgestellt ist, stammt aus der Michaelerkirche. Es kann angenommen werden, daß die Aufführungen von Mozarts Requiem KV 626 in dieser Kirche mit dieser Posaune gespielt wurden.“ He seems to say, then that the second, identical trombone (1738-2) came from the same church, and that it is now in the National Library. Note: Stradner 1991: 295 lists “Posaunendämpfer” Austria, end of 17 cen to ca. 1750. Walnut. L 130; D 52.
remarks: Tubular slide-stays. Flat bell-stay, engraved, with eyelet, hinge with pin on bell-pipe side. Sleeves round with ring pattern. Associated case of walnut with with iron fittings. Case H 120, L 870: B 135.
